From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## 1. Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim

The cover note says these positions were settled by both deal teams at principal level, are marked FINAL, and reflect "market" terms. Treat this as an unverified assertion by the other side.

- Our file shows no written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback. That covers the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and the 18-month period, both of which the Seller has adopted.
- The Seller's "market" figures are advocacy, not a basis for conceding anything.
- **Action:** Confirm with Amelia Frost that nothing was agreed at principal level. Reply that all positions remain open and subject to contract. Don't let silence be read as acceptance.

## 2. Departures from the playbook

### A. Liability architecture

| Item | Seller draft | Our position | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m | This is exactly our conditional fallback, which we lack authority to use. Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded | 5x higher and a deductible, not a tipping basket. Together with the de minimis, this could screen out most realistic claims. |
| General period (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months | Our fallback, and no approval has been given. |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. "Administrative simplicity" would cut title protection from roughly 100% to 20%. |
| Limitation scope (12.3/13) | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise | Categories kept separate, no hidden general-regime override | This default-to-general wording is the hidden override the playbook prohibits. It should be reversed so limits apply only where expressly stated. |

### B. Fraud and misconduct (the most serious structural defect)

Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature". There is no carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. That would limit or exclude liability for deliberate wrongdoing. Our playbook requires the carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive it. This is a non-negotiable. Fundamental, title and specific-indemnity claims should also sit outside these clauses.

### C. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

- **Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2:** The letter discloses the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. This is the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure we reject. We require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties.
- **Clause 8.3:** This excludes anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. It is constructive knowledge. Combined with general disclosure, it largely removes warranty protection. Delete it. If the Seller needs a qualifier, the only acceptable form is named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Staleness:** The data-room cut-off is 5.00pm 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November. Require updated disclosure and a bring-down to Completion, and don't treat later-arising matters as disclosed.
- **Letter 1.4 (non-admission):** This is acceptable as a reservation, but it should not operate as a limit on warranty or indemnity claims.

### D. Conditions and Completion mechanics

**Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m, about 30% of FY26 revenue)**
- The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and treats the consent as satisfied on delivery.
- The Seller's own letter (item 2) admits there is no final written consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are met, so "addressed" is inaccurate.
- Required: a condition precedent of effective consent, plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this weight.
- Consent on delivery is not enough, because a consent with unsatisfied conditions may be ineffective.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m outstanding)**
- The Seller proposes a release after Completion. Its own letter (item 3) confirms no repayment and no discharge of security.
- Required: a current payout figure (the "approximately" figure is not enough), direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- A post-completion release is available only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists.
- This is a debt-free deal, so the payout should come off the price flow.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000 plus on-costs)**
- The Seller says it is "a matter for the Seller" and leaves it out of the funds flow. Its letter (item 5) confirms it is absent and silent on payroll tax, super and other on-costs.
- Required: a specific line item in the funds flow, or an express Seller-funded mechanism. The on-costs need to be quantified, and we shouldn't guess the figure.
- The funds flow must not silently exclude them.

### E. Specific matters

- **Ironquay IP (cl 11.1):** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment.
  - Broaden it beyond the payment to the underlying IP risk, for example loss from the Project Materials not transferring and related claims. Preserve the SOW3 cure.
  - The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified in either direction. DD-010 records it as open, but the Seller's letter itself says that is not bank verification. Don't assert it is owed or paid. Request payment evidence or a confirmatory assignment.
- **DD-006 export/privacy incident:** The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material".
  - That characterisation is unsupported. The Seller's own letter says the material doesn't establish access, scope or notification duty.
  - We shouldn't swing the other way either. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
  - Required: preservation of logs, a continuing investigation, and update and cooperation covenants. Don't accept any wording that deems the matter immaterial or resolved.
- **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000, three at AUD 110,000):** "Ordinary-course" is asserted, not supported. The letter (item 8) doesn't say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
  - Assess terms, timing and terminability.
  - There should be no automatic Debt classification or price deduction, and no concession that they are ordinary course.
- **Tax and IP:** The Seller treats these as "settled under the general regime". They are open. Reject that and keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate. Don't assume unlimited liability or any resolution on either side.
- **Title:** The Seller relies on the DD-012 register. That is a supplied internal source, not independent proof, and the Seller's own letter (item 10) concedes it doesn't show our verification.
  - Require independent evidence of ownership, encumbrances and authority.
  - Include a check on whether Riverlark's security touches the shares.
  - Capacity and title warranties belong in the fundamental regime (see A).
- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller's letter says neither provision states that consent is required for a share sale. That is the Seller's reading of the documents, so confirm it in our own review. We have no playbook position beyond that.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Immediate**
1. Confirm with Amelia Frost that nothing was agreed at principal level. State to the Seller that all positions are open and subject to contract.
2. Do not use the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks. If the team wants to consider either, Amelia must give written authority identifying the specific draft. None exists today.

**Mark-up positions to reject outright (non-negotiable)**
- The fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct gap in 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5. Add a full carve-out.
- Fundamental and title claims under the general caps and time limits. Restore the separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Clause 8.3 buyer knowledge, including advisers and "discoverable" matters.
- Whole-data-room, public-register and Accounts deemed disclosure. Replace with specific fair disclosure.
- The "limitation applies to all Claims" default, and the claim that Tax and IP are settled under the general regime.

**Counter-proposals**
- Cap 25% / AUD 6m, de minimis AUD 5,000, basket AUD 50,000 first-dollar, general period 24 months.
- Bluefen: CP of effective consent plus evidence the conditions are met before Completion.
- Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and security releases effective at Completion.
- Bonuses: a specific funds-flow line for AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs, or an express Seller-funded mechanism.
- Ironquay: a broader IP indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure, with payment evidence requested.
- DD-006: preservation, investigation and update covenants. No characterisation of the matter.
- Title: independent verification package, with DD-012 treated as a starting point only.

**Assess before positioning**
- Sandbar: review terms and terminability. No concession on Debt or price either way.
- Lease and Mossvale: verify the consent position independently.
- Request updated disclosure with a bring-down, given the 22 September cut-off.

**Useful leverage:** The Seller's own letter admits there is no Bluefen consent or conditions evidence, no Riverlark repayment or discharge, no Ironquay payment receipt, and no bonuses in the funds flow. Their cover note's "addressed" and "agreed" language is contradicted by their own disclosure, and we can use this when we push back.
